calls.title: Experiment Creation / Add FF
calls.summary: The team focused on improving the feature flag and variation management setup. They proposed consolidating variations and feature values into a unified table to enhance clarity and reduce context switching. Editable metadata will be integrated into the core interface while keeping additional details in a separate panel to minimize clutter. The design allows for managing multiple feature flags and emphasizes the experiment as the source of truth for active environments. Additionally, the introduction of a validation modal will confirm necessary configurations before starting an experiment, enhancing overall accuracy. The group also discussed integrating draft and live feature states, prioritizing visibility, and establishing an incremental approach to implementing these changes.
calls.keywords: feature flags, experiment creation, variation configuration, traffic split, UI design, approval flow

calls.title: Experiment Creation / Add FF
calls.summary: The team discussed centralizing feature flag value management on the experiment page to reduce user confusion and establish a clearer workflow. Luke Sonnet emphasized making the experiment page the 'source of truth,' facilitating better targeting and value settings. Bryce Fitzsimons highlighted the necessity for a unified approval process for changes affecting both experiment and feature settings to prevent redundancy. Adriel Vieira proposed linking feature flag lifecycles to those of experiments, ensuring consistent behavior during reversions. The team also acknowledged the need to simplify environment-specific configurations and emphasized the importance of notifying feature owners about any experiment-driven changes. Lastly, they prioritized fixing linked features data inconsistencies to improve reliability and user experience.
calls.keywords: Feature Flags, Experiment Page, Approval Flow, Draft Revisions, Environment Configuration, Payload Management
